digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI

teaser.en: The 'male' *mwangajine* has huge leaves and large cream flowers, and like its namesake it is a medicine for spiritual illness.

summary.en: *Mwangajine mlume* is a large-leaved shrub or small tree of evergreen coastal forest, often on coral rock. It is a spiritual medicine, like the *mwangajine* it is named after, and it is listed as Vulnerable.

about.en: *Mwangajine mlume* is a shrub or small tree with very large leaves, long and broad, which make it stand out in the forest undergrowth. Its flowers are large and cream-coloured, thick-petalled in the way of the custard-apple family.

where.en: It grows in evergreen coastal forest, often on coral rock.

uses.en: It is used as a spiritual medicine, in the same way as *mwangajine*.

culture.en: The name is explained as 'male spirit-being': this is the large-leaved *mwangajine*, the male partner to *mwangajine* (*Isolona cauliflora*). Both carry the names of the spirits Mwanga and Jine.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mwangajine mlume* and *mzondohera nguluwe*. Duruma shares the name *mwangajine*. No Swahili or English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Uvariodendron kirkii*. *Mzondohera nguluwe* is also recorded as the Digo name of a different shrub, the sandpaper saucer-berry (*Cordia monoica*).

conservation.en: *Mwangajine mlume* is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List and depends on the remaining evergreen coastal forest.

reason.en: The 'female' partner, also a spiritual medicine
Named after the same spirit, Mwanga
Mkilua, same custard-apple family, also Vulnerable
